questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the process view of a supply chain?

options.A: It explains only the financial performance of a firm.
options.B: It shows how supply chain activities flow across partners such as customers, retailers, distributors, manufacturers and suppliers
options.C: It focuses only on transportation and warehousing decisions.
options.D: It explains only long-term supply chain design decisions.

questions.explanation: The process view maps out how activities, decisions, and material/information flows occur continuously across different supply chain stages—from suppliers down to end customers.

questions.question_text: Why are supply chain performance drivers and KPIs important?

options.A: They remove the need for planning and coordination.
options.B: They focus only on reducing transportation costs.
options.C: They help understand how decisions affect cost, service, speed, reliability and overall performance.
options.D: They are used only for financial reporting.

questions.explanation: Performance drivers and KPIs allow managers to evaluate operational trade-offs and assess how choices in facilities, inventory, transportation, sourcing, pricing, and information impact financial health and service levels.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to understand demand components before choosing a forecasting method?

options.A: It helps managers avoid using past demand data.
options.B: It helps managers identify patterns such as level, trend, seasonality and random variation.
options.C: It removes the need to measure forecast error.
options.D: It ensures that demand will always remain stable.

questions.explanation: Identifying underlying patterns like trend, level, seasonality, and random noise enables managers to select the appropriate quantitative model (e.g., Simple Exponential Smoothing vs. Holt's Method or Multiplicative Seasonality).

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains why inventory decisions involve trade-offs?

options.A: More inventory always improves supply chain performance
options.B: Inventory helps manage uncertainty and service levels, but it also creates costs such as holding cost and obsolescence
options.C: Inventory decisions are only about reducing purchase cost
options.D: ABC classification removes the need for inventory planning

questions.explanation: Carrying inventory buffers against demand uncertainty and lead-time delays to achieve high product availability, but higher stock levels increase carrying/holding costs, capital lockup, and risk of product obsolescence.

questions.question_text: A firm is sourcing two products. Product A has stable demand, high volume and a mature design. Product B has uncertain demand, frequent design changes and high stockout risk. Which sourcing approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Use only one low-cost offshore supplier for both products
options.B: Use a low-cost source for Product A and a responsive source for Product B
options.C: Use only onshore suppliers for both products
options.D: Avoid supplier evaluation and select the lowest quoted price

questions.explanation: Tailored sourcing matches supplier capabilities to demand characteristics: predictable, high-volume products (Product A) benefit from efficient, low-cost sources, while volatile, high-risk products (Product B) require flexible, responsive sources.
